=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Date:** 5 November 2026
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

---

## 0. Preliminary point – the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's package ends with a note stating that clauses tagged [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny", that the disclosure framework and limitation package are "already accepted", and that review should focus only on [OPEN] items (there are none).

**We should disregard this entirely.** Nothing in our instructions indicates Wattlebridge has agreed any of these positions. The tags were applied unilaterally by the Seller, and the items marked [STANDARD] are in fact the most buyer-adverse provisions in the package (liability caps on title warranties, knowledge exclusions, the Riverlark release timing, the bonus funds-flow omission). The note is a drafting device to narrow our review; it has no contractual effect and should not be allowed to anchor the negotiation. I have reviewed every provision below on its merits. Recommend the response letter expressly records that no clause has been "cleared" and that all positions remain open.

---

## 1. Liability regime (cl. 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

### 1.1 General cap – 20% / AUD 4.8m
A 20% cap is at the low end for an Australian private M&A deal of this size; 25–50% is a more typical range for a buyer without W&I insurance. More importantly, the cap is proposed to apply to *everything* (see 1.3). On its own, 20% may be negotiable upward depending on whether we are pursuing W&I; if we are not, push for 50% on general warranties, and in any event ensure the specific indemnities and the Riverlark/bonus/Sandbar price adjustments sit outside the cap.

### 1.2 De minimis and basket
AUD 25,000 de minimis (0.1% of price) and AUD 250,000 basket (~1%) are within market, but two points:
- **Excess-only recovery** ("only the excess above the basket is recoverable"). We should push for a **tipping basket** (once exceeded, recovery from dollar one). This is a common ask and usually conceded or split.
- Confirm that related claims arising from the same facts aggregate for the de minimis, so the Seller cannot fragment a systemic issue into sub-AUD 25k pieces.

### 1.3 "All limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" – **reject**
This is the single most important structural point. Combined with cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 ("limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature"), the effect is that:
- Title/capacity warranty claims are capped at 20% and barred after 18 months;
- Tax warranty claims are capped and barred after 18 months (well inside the ATO's 4-year amendment period, let alone fraud/evasion periods);
- Specific indemnities (Ironquay, and any we negotiate for DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark) are swept into the cap, basket and de minimis;
- Fraud, wilful concealment and dishonesty are not carved out;
- Price-adjustment / leakage / completion-accounts claims are arguably caught.

**Position:** The limitations must apply to general Warranty Claims only, with express carve-outs for (a) Fundamental Warranties (title, capacity, authority, no insolvency) – cap at 100% of price, time limit 6 years or the statutory limitation period; (b) Tax Warranties and the Tax Indemnity – cap 100%, time limit 7 years after Completion (or 4 years after the last relevant amendment period); (c) all specific indemnities – uncapped or separately capped, no de minimis/basket; (d) fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment – no limitation at all; (e) leakage / completion adjustments – separate regime. The "unless expressly stated otherwise" wording must be flipped so that the default is that carve-outs stand unless a limitation is expressly stated to apply.

### 1.4 Fundamental/title warranties "subject to the same caps for administrative simplicity" – **reject**
There is no administrative burden in a separate cap; this is purely a risk-transfer ask. If title fails, our loss is the whole AUD 24m; a 20% cap leaves us with AUD 4.8m. Not acceptable.

### 1.5 18-month time limit
18 months is at the short end but acceptable **for general warranties only** if we obtain the carve-outs above; it will typically allow us to see one full audit cycle post-Completion. If we cannot get a full set of carve-outs, push general claims to 24 months.

### 1.6 Exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl. 12.8 / 20.5)
Non-reliance clauses are standard but should not exclude (i) the express SPA terms, (ii) fraud, or (iii) statutory rights that cannot be excluded (misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law / ASIC Act – a purported exclusion is of doubtful effect and the Seller should not be allowed to argue we have agreed to it). The exclusive-remedy clause should not exclude equitable relief (specific performance, injunction) for breach of restraints and pre-Completion covenants.

---

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge (Schedule 7, cl. 8.3, DL paras 1.1–1.4)

### 2.1 General disclosure of the entire data room and "publicly searchable corporate records" – **reject / narrow**
Para 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the data room. Para 1.2 adds public registers. This is a blanket disclosure that converts every document into a qualification of every warranty, regardless of whether the risk was apparent.

**Position:** Disclosure must be **"fair disclosure"** – disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter disclosed. Data room disclosure should be limited to the contents of the indexed data room as at an agreed cut-off (and a USB/download of it should be annexed to the SPA and initialled). Delete the public-register limb, or limit it to ASIC company searches of the Company itself at a fixed date; "publicly searchable corporate records" is unbounded (court lists, PPSR, IP registers, OAIC, land titles, overseas registers).

### 2.2 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge exclusion – **reject**
"No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" is far wider than a knowledge clause:
- "Discoverable" is constructive knowledge – we are deemed to know everything a perfect diligence process would have found, whether or not we did.
- "Advisers" imputes knowledge of every lawyer, accountant, and technical consultant engaged, without any requirement that it was communicated to the deal team.
- It operates in addition to the disclosure regime, so matters that are *not* fairly disclosed are nonetheless excluded if arguably "discoverable".

**Position:** Delete cl. 8.3. If a knowledge clause must survive, limit it to actual knowledge of a named list of 3–4 individuals on the Wattlebridge deal team, of facts fairly disclosed, with no imputation of adviser knowledge and no constructive-knowledge limb. Note that in NSW, actual-knowledge clauses have been enforced; the Seller will push for this, so the key fight is deleting "discoverable" and "advisers".

### 2.3 Para 1.4 – non-admission
Standard, but it should not be allowed to undercut specific indemnities. Make clear that disclosure of a matter does not prevent a claim under a specific indemnity for that matter (the indemnity should be drafted "notwithstanding any disclosure").

### 2.4 Para 11 – reservation
The Seller disclaims any conclusions and puts the onus on us to evaluate. That is fine as a statement, but it reinforces that the Seller is deliberately not warranting the *characterisation* of any of the items below. Our response is to convert each one into a specific warranty, specific indemnity, condition precedent, or price adjustment rather than relying on general warranties qualified by disclosure.

---

## 3. Transaction-specific issues

Each issue below is marked by the Seller as [STANDARD] or "not material". On the disclosed facts, each one is material.

### 3.1 Bluefen (DD-002) – ~AUD 3.6m revenue, ~30% of FY26
- Seller: "reasonable endeavours" and the condition is satisfied on "delivery of the counterparty's written consent".
- Disclosure Letter para 2: **no final written consent** and **no evidence conditions in cl. 11.3 are satisfied**.

Problems:
- "Reasonable endeavours" is the lowest standard; for a customer representing 30% of revenue we need **all reasonable endeavours** or **best endeavours**, with a positive obligation to procure the consent and to keep us informed and involved in the discussions.
- Satisfaction "on delivery of written consent" ignores the 11.3 conditions. A consent that is itself conditional (e.g. on price concessions, change of terms, a right to re-tender, or a termination right exercisable post-Completion) is not a satisfied condition.

**Position:** Condition precedent for Buyer's benefit: Bluefen written consent, **unconditional** or on conditions satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably), with evidence that all cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied; no amendment to Bluefen commercial terms without Buyer approval; Buyer to be party to the consent discussion. Add a specific warranty that the Bluefen contract is in full force, not subject to any notice of termination or re-tender, and no price concession has been offered. Consider a price adjustment or earn-out/retention (e.g. AUD 1.5–2.0m held for 12 months) if the consent is delivered conditionally. If no consent, Buyer right to terminate.

### 3.2 Riverlark Bank facility (DD-003) – ~AUD 3.2m outstanding
- Seller: release "to be provided **following** Completion".
- Disclosure: **not repaid, no discharge of security**, change-of-control at 8.1.

This is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal and is a direct AUD 3.2m value point:
- If the facility remains outstanding at Completion, the Company (now ours) owes AUD 3.2m and the bank holds security over the business we have just paid AUD 24m for.
- A change-of-control clause at 8.1 means the bank can accelerate on Completion unless consent is obtained.
- A "release following Completion" leaves us holding default risk and relying on the Seller's post-Completion cooperation.

**Position:** Repayment and release at Completion, not after. Mechanically: (i) the facility balance (principal, interest, break costs, fees as per a bank payout letter dated the Completion date) is deducted from the price / paid directly from the purchase monies to Riverlark under the funds flow; (ii) Completion deliverables include the executed deed of release, PPSR discharge/financing change statement, release of any guarantees from the Company, and release of any mortgage; (iii) if the Seller insists on a post-Completion release, an escrow of at least the outstanding balance plus a buffer, with a Seller indemnity for any amount payable under the facility. Confirm there are no other debt-like items (guarantees, hire purchase, related-party loans) by requiring a schedule of Indebtedness and a cl. 2/7 price adjustment for any Indebtedness at Completion.

### 3.3 Closing bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420,000 plus on-costs
- Seller: "a matter for the Seller and not separately itemised in the funds flow".
- Disclosure: conditional on Completion and continued employment; on-costs (super, payroll tax) **not stated**.

If the bonuses are payable by the **Company** (which is the usual structure), they become our cost the day after Completion. Under a debt-free/cash-free deal, transaction-triggered employee payments are Transaction Costs / debt-like items. Superannuation on bonuses (12% SG from 1 July 2025) and NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) add roughly AUD 70–75k, plus potential Fringe Benefits/PAYG withholding mechanics.

**Position:** Bonuses, super, payroll tax and employer on-costs must be itemised in the funds flow and either (a) paid by the Seller directly, or (b) deducted from the purchase price (grossed up for on-costs), with a specific indemnity for any amount not so dealt with. Obtain the bonus letters; check whether "continued employment" conditions are 'as at Completion' (cost is crystallised) or a retention period (then a retention mechanism may be appropriate and the cost should still sit with the Seller). Confirm no other change-of-control triggers (options, phantom equity, acceleration of LTI).

### 3.4 Ironquay Development Studio (DD-004 / DD-010) – IP ownership
- Seller: existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
- Disclosure: cl. 7.3 transfers SOW3 Project Materials **only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**; AUD 180,000 shown as open; no receipt, no confirmatory assignment.

This is not a AUD 180k issue – it is a **title-to-IP issue**. If SOW3 fees are unpaid, Ironquay (not Paperbark) owns the SOW3 Project Materials. If those materials are embedded in the analytics platform, we are buying software the Company does not own, with an exposed developer who can withhold assignment or injunct. An indemnity capped at AUD 180k does not address loss of IP, re-development cost, or customer liability.

**Position:**
- Condition precedent (or Completion deliverable): evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and** an executed confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay of all Project Materials (all SOWs, not just SOW3), with moral rights consents from the developers.
- Specific warranty: the Company owns all IP in the platform; no third-party contractor retains any interest.
- Specific indemnity, uncapped or capped at the purchase price, for all loss arising from any failure to own the Ironquay-developed materials, including re-development and customer claims.
- Diligence action: our tech team should confirm what SOW3 delivered and how deeply it is integrated.

### 3.5 Data export / privacy incident (DD-006) – ~1,240 records
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- Disclosure: download link sent to an unintended external address; records include names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps; unknown whether accessed; unknown whether notification required; investigation "preliminary" as at 22 September.

This is a potential eligible data breach under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Notifiable Data Breaches scheme). Note the **statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy** (in force since June 2025), the expanded civil penalty tiers (including the new mid-tier and lower-tier penalties), and OAIC's increased enforcement posture. Business contact details of ~1,240 individuals, combined with activity data, are personal information; depending on the records, they may be customer-contract data subject to contractual confidentiality and notification obligations (including potentially Bluefen's). A six-week-old "preliminary" investigation is itself a concern: the NDB regime expects assessment within 30 days.

**Position:**
- Pre-Completion covenant: Seller to procure that the Company completes the assessment (and, if required, OAIC and individual notification) before Completion, with the Buyer given the investigation report, the link-recall/access logs, and copies of any notifications.
- Specific warranty on privacy compliance and on this incident (scope, access, notification status).
- Specific indemnity for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident, including regulatory penalties, investigation costs, customer claims, notification costs and remediation, outside the cap/basket/de minimis and with a 6-year time limit.
- Confirm the Company's cyber insurance position and whether the insurer has been notified.

### 3.6 Office lease (DD-007)
Seller frames it as a notification obligation only. Accept the framing provisionally, but: (i) obtain the lease and confirm there is no "change in control" deemed assignment clause (common in commercial leases), (ii) add a Completion deliverable that the required notice has been given, and (iii) warranty that no landlord consent is required and no breach exists.

### 3.7 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – AUD 330,000
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs.
- Disclosure: three related renewals of AUD 110k each; **"read together for timing/scope"**; disclosure silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

The "read together" cue suggests the renewals may have been split to sit under an approval threshold, or that they are timed around Completion. Key questions: are the renewals multi-year commitments, were they entered into after the Accounts date (and so are they leakage or a working-capital point), is there an auto-renewal already triggered, and are they above-market/related-party?

**Position:** Obtain the three renewal documents and supplier relationship details. Treat any commitments entered into between the Accounts date and Completion outside the ordinary course as Leakage / subject to Buyer consent under the pre-Completion conduct covenants. If accrued but unpaid at Completion, they should be in the working-capital/debt-like calculation. Add a warranty on no splitting of contracts to avoid thresholds and that supplier contracts are at arm's length.

### 3.8 Mossvale (DD-009)
Seller says the assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. That is generally correct for a pure anti-assignment clause, but we should read DD-009 ourselves to confirm there is no change-of-control or "deemed assignment" limb. Warranty that no consent is required under any Material Contract other than those listed; indemnity if the Mossvale counterparty terminates on the basis of the transaction.

### 3.9 Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" – **reject**
This is an attempt to fold tax and IP into the 20%/18-month regime. Tax requires a separate Tax Indemnity (pre-Completion tax of the Company, including under any income tax consolidated group exit, GST, payroll tax, stamp duty on the sale, and R&D tax incentive clawbacks given this is an analytics business) with a 100% cap and a 7-year limit. IP needs its own Fundamental-style treatment given the Ironquay point. Also confirm: (i) whether Paperbark is a member of the Harbourglass tax consolidated group and, if so, the clear exit mechanics and tax sharing/funding agreement; (ii) NSW duty position on the share acquisition (landholder duty is unlikely for an analytics business but should be confirmed).

### 3.10 Title (DD-012) – share register only
The Seller's evidence of title is the Company's own share register, and para 10 expressly notes the Buyer has not verified it. We should: (i) obtain an ASIC current extract and compare members/share structure; (ii) obtain the constitution and any shareholders' agreement to check pre-emptive rights and transfer restrictions; (iii) PPSR search against both the Company and Harbourglass for security over the shares (Riverlark may hold a share mortgage); (iv) confirm there are no options, convertible notes, SAFE instruments or employee equity; (v) obtain executed share transfer form, share certificate (or statement of non-issue), and board resolutions approving registration at Completion. Title warranties must be Fundamental (100% cap, 6 years).

---

## 4. Funds flow and price mechanics

"The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics" is not accurate on the Seller's own disclosure. Debt-free/cash-free means the AUD 24m is an enterprise value to be adjusted at Completion. The draft funds flow omits:
- Riverlark repayment (~AUD 3.2m) – should be a deduction and a direct payment to the bank;
- Closing bonuses and on-costs (~AUD 490k+) – deduction or Seller-paid;
- Potentially the Ironquay SOW3 open amount (AUD 180k) if paid at Completion to perfect IP;
- Any accrued Sandbar liabilities;
- Transaction costs borne by the Company.

We need a locked-box (with leakage protection and a per-diem charge) or completion-accounts mechanism actually drafted into cl. 2/7 with defined Cash, Debt, Debt-like items and Working Capital, and a schedule of agreed Debt-like items. On the current draft we would pay AUD 24m headline and inherit ~AUD 3.9m of debt-like items.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

**Threshold:**
1. Reject the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"; record in writing that nothing is agreed and all clauses remain open.

**Liability regime:**
2. Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Carve out Fundamental/Title, Tax, specific indemnities, fraud/wilful concealment, and price adjustments.
3. Fundamental and Tax: 100% cap; 6 years (Fundamental) / 7 years (Tax).
4. General cap: open at 50%, settle no lower than 30% absent W&I.
5. Tipping basket; aggregation of related claims for de minimis.
6. Non-reliance/exclusive remedy: carve out fraud, express SPA terms, non-excludable statutory rights, equitable relief.

**Disclosure and knowledge:**
7. "Fair disclosure" standard; data room frozen and annexed; delete public-register general disclosure.
8. Delete cl. 8.3. Fall-back: actual knowledge of named individuals only; no "discoverable", no adviser imputation.
9. Specific indemnities to apply "notwithstanding any disclosure".

**Deal-specific:**
10. **Bluefen:** CP for unconditional consent (11.3 conditions satisfied); all reasonable endeavours; Buyer involvement; retention/adjustment if conditional; termination right.
11. **Riverlark:** repay and release *at* Completion from purchase monies via payout letter; release deeds and PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables; escrow if not.
12. **Bonuses:** itemise bonuses plus super/payroll tax in funds flow; Seller cost; indemnity.
13. **Ironquay:** CP/deliverable – proof of SOW3 payment and confirmatory IP assignment with moral rights consents; IP ownership warranty; uncapped specific indemnity.
14. **DD-006:** complete NDB assessment/notification pre-Completion; disclosure of report; specific warranty and uncapped indemnity.
15. **Sandbar:** obtain the documents; treat as leakage/working-capital unless shown to be ordinary course; anti-splitting warranty.
16. **Tax/IP:** separate Tax Indemnity and Tax Warranties; consolidated-group exit mechanics; stamp duty confirmation.
17. **Title:** independent verification (ASIC, constitution, PPSR, shareholders' agreement, no dilutive instruments); Fundamental treatment.
18. **Lease/Mossvale:** confirm no change-of-control limb; notification deliverable; warranty on required consents.

**Price mechanics:**
19. Replace the funds flow with a proper debt-free/cash-free adjustment (locked box with leakage, or completion accounts), expressly deducting Riverlark, bonuses and on-costs, and any other Debt-like items; schedule of agreed Debt-like items annexed.

**Diligence follow-ups before we respond:** Bluefen cl. 11.2–11.3 and consent correspondence; Riverlark facility and security documents; Ironquay SOW3 and tech integration assessment; DD-005 bonus letters; DD-006 investigation status and insurance notification; Sandbar renewal documents; constitution/shareholders' agreement and ASIC/PPSR searches.

Let me know if you would like me to turn this into a formal mark-up of the SPA clauses or a response letter to Harbourglass's counsel.

This is the single most important structural point. Combined with cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 ("limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature"), the effect is that:
- Title/capacity warranty claims are capped at 20% and barred after 18 months;
- Tax warranty claims are capped and barred after 18 months (well inside the ATO's 4-year amendment period, let alone fraud/evasion periods);
- Specific indemnities (Ironquay, and any we negotiate for DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark) are swept into the cap, basket and de minimis;
- Fraud, wilful concealment and dishonesty are not carved out;
- Price-adjustment / leakage / completion-accounts claims are arguably caught.

**Position:** The limitations must apply to general Warranty Claims only, with express carve-outs for (a) Fundamental Warranties (title, capacity, authority, no insolvency) – cap at 100% of price, time limit 6 years or the statutory limitation period; (b) Tax Warranties and the Tax Indemnity – cap 100%, time limit 7 years after Completion (or 4 years after the last relevant amendment period); (c) all specific indemnities – uncapped or separately capped, no de minimis/basket; (d) fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment – no limitation at all; (e) leakage / completion adjustments – separate regime. The "unless expressly stated otherwise" wording must be flipped so that the default is that carve-outs stand unless a limitation is expressly stated to apply.

### 1.4 Fundamental/title warranties "subject to the same caps for administrative simplicity" – **reject**
There is no administrative burden in a separate cap; this is purely a risk-transfer ask. If title fails, our loss is the whole AUD 24m; a 20% cap leaves us with AUD 4.8m. Not acceptable.

### 1.5 18-month time limit
18 months is at the short end but acceptable **for general warranties only** if we obtain the carve-outs above; it will typically allow us to see one full audit cycle post-Completion. If we cannot get a full set of carve-outs, push general claims to 24 months.

### 1.6 Exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl. 12.8 / 20.5)
Non-reliance clauses are standard but should not exclude (i) the express SPA terms, (ii) fraud, or (iii) statutory rights that cannot be excluded (misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law / ASIC Act – a purported exclusion is of doubtful effect and the Seller should not be allowed to argue we have agreed to it). The exclusive-remedy clause should not exclude equitable relief (specific performance, injunction) for breach of restraints and pre-Completion covenants.

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge (Schedule 7, cl. 8.3, DL paras 1.1–1.4)

### 2.1 General disclosure of the entire data room and "publicly searchable corporate records" – **reject / narrow**
Para 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the data room. Para 1.2 adds public registers. This is a blanket disclosure that converts every document into a qualification of every warranty, regardless of whether the risk was apparent.

**Position:** Disclosure must be **"fair disclosure"** – disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter disclosed. Data room disclosure should be limited to the contents of the indexed data room as at an agreed cut-off (and a USB/download of it should be annexed to the SPA and initialled). Delete the public-register limb, or limit it to ASIC company searches of the Company itself at a fixed date; "publicly searchable corporate records" is unbounded (court lists, PPSR, IP registers, OAIC, land titles, overseas registers).

### 2.2 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge exclusion – **reject**
"No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" is far wider than a knowledge clause:
- "Discoverable" is constructive knowledge – we are deemed to know everything a perfect diligence process would have found, whether or not we did.
- "Advisers" imputes knowledge of every lawyer, accountant, and technical consultant engaged, without any requirement that it was communicated to the deal team.
- It operates in addition to the disclosure regime, so matters that are *not* fairly disclosed are nonetheless excluded if arguably "discoverable".

**Position:** Delete cl. 8.3. If a knowledge clause must survive, limit it to actual knowledge of a named list of 3–4 individuals on the Wattlebridge deal team, of facts fairly disclosed, with no imputation of adviser knowledge and no constructive-knowledge limb. Note that in NSW, actual-knowledge clauses have been enforced; the Seller will push for this, so the key fight is deleting "discoverable" and "advisers".

### 2.3 Para 1.4 – non-admission
Standard, but it should not be allowed to undercut specific indemnities. Make clear that disclosure of a matter does not prevent a claim under a specific indemnity for that matter (the indemnity should be drafted "notwithstanding any disclosure").

### 2.4 Para 11 – reservation
The Seller disclaims any conclusions and puts the onus on us to evaluate. That is fine as a statement, but it reinforces that the Seller is deliberately not warranting the *characterisation* of any of the items below. Our response is to convert each one into a specific warranty, specific indemnity, condition precedent, or price adjustment rather than relying on general warranties qualified by disclosure.

## 3. Transaction-specific issues

Each issue below is marked by the Seller as [STANDARD] or "not material". On the disclosed facts, each one is material.

### 3.1 Bluefen (DD-002) – ~AUD 3.6m revenue, ~30% of FY26
- Seller: "reasonable endeavours" and the condition is satisfied on "delivery of the counterparty's written consent".
- Disclosure Letter para 2: **no final written consent** and **no evidence conditions in cl. 11.3 are satisfied**.

Problems:
- "Reasonable endeavours" is the lowest standard; for a customer representing 30% of revenue we need **all reasonable endeavours** or **best endeavours**, with a positive obligation to procure the consent and to keep us informed and involved in the discussions.
- Satisfaction "on delivery of written consent" ignores the 11.3 conditions. A consent that is itself conditional (e.g. on price concessions, change of terms, a right to re-tender, or a termination right exercisable post-Completion) is not a satisfied condition.

**Position:** Condition precedent for Buyer's benefit: Bluefen written consent, **unconditional** or on conditions satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably), with evidence that all cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied; no amendment to Bluefen commercial terms without Buyer approval; Buyer to be party to the consent discussion. Add a specific warranty that the Bluefen contract is in full force, not subject to any notice of termination or re-tender, and no price concession has been offered. Consider a price adjustment or earn-out/retention (e.g. AUD 1.5–2.0m held for 12 months) if the consent is delivered conditionally. If no consent, Buyer right to terminate.

### 3.2 Riverlark Bank facility (DD-003) – ~AUD 3.2m outstanding
- Seller: release "to be provided **following** Completion".
- Disclosure: **not repaid, no discharge of security**, change-of-control at 8.1.

This is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal and is a direct AUD 3.2m value point:
- If the facility remains outstanding at Completion, the Company (now ours) owes AUD 3.2m and the bank holds security over the business we have just paid AUD 24m for.
- A change-of-control clause at 8.1 means the bank can accelerate on Completion unless consent is obtained.
- A "release following Completion" leaves us holding default risk and relying on the Seller's post-Completion cooperation.

**Position:** Repayment and release at Completion, not after. Mechanically: (i) the facility balance (principal, interest, break costs, fees as per a bank payout letter dated the Completion date) is deducted from the price / paid directly from the purchase monies to Riverlark under the funds flow; (ii) Completion deliverables include the executed deed of release, PPSR discharge/financing change statement, release of any guarantees from the Company, and release of any mortgage; (iii) if the Seller insists on a post-Completion release, an escrow of at least the outstanding balance plus a buffer, with a Seller indemnity for any amount payable under the facility. Confirm there are no other debt-like items (guarantees, hire purchase, related-party loans) by requiring a schedule of Indebtedness and a cl. 2/7 price adjustment for any Indebtedness at Completion.

### 3.3 Closing bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420,000 plus on-costs
- Seller: "a matter for the Seller and not separately itemised in the funds flow".
- Disclosure: conditional on Completion and continued employment; on-costs (super, payroll tax) **not stated**.

If the bonuses are payable by the **Company** (which is the usual structure), they become our cost the day after Completion. Under a debt-free/cash-free deal, transaction-triggered employee payments are Transaction Costs / debt-like items. Superannuation on bonuses (12% SG from 1 July 2025) and NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) add roughly AUD 70–75k, plus potential Fringe Benefits/PAYG withholding mechanics.

**Position:** Bonuses, super, payroll tax and employer on-costs must be itemised in the funds flow and either (a) paid by the Seller directly, or (b) deducted from the purchase price (grossed up for on-costs), with a specific indemnity for any amount not so dealt with. Obtain the bonus letters; check whether "continued employment" conditions are 'as at Completion' (cost is crystallised) or a retention period (then a retention mechanism may be appropriate and the cost should still sit with the Seller). Confirm no other change-of-control triggers (options, phantom equity, acceleration of LTI).

### 3.4 Ironquay Development Studio (DD-004 / DD-010) – IP ownership
- Seller: existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
- Disclosure: cl. 7.3 transfers SOW3 Project Materials **only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**; AUD 180,000 shown as open; no receipt, no confirmatory assignment.

This is not a AUD 180k issue – it is a **title-to-IP issue**. If SOW3 fees are unpaid, Ironquay (not Paperbark) owns the SOW3 Project Materials. If those materials are embedded in the analytics platform, we are buying software the Company does not own, with an exposed developer who can withhold assignment or injunct. An indemnity capped at AUD 180k does not address loss of IP, re-development cost, or customer liability.

**Position:**
- Condition precedent (or Completion deliverable): evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and** an executed confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay of all Project Materials (all SOWs, not just SOW3), with moral rights consents from the developers.
- Specific warranty: the Company owns all IP in the platform; no third-party contractor retains any interest.
- Specific indemnity, uncapped or capped at the purchase price, for all loss arising from any failure to own the Ironquay-developed materials, including re-development and customer claims.
- Diligence action: our tech team should confirm what SOW3 delivered and how deeply it is integrated.

### 3.5 Data export / privacy incident (DD-006) – ~1,240 records
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- Disclosure: download link sent to an unintended external address; records include names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps; unknown whether accessed; unknown whether notification required; investigation "preliminary" as at 22 September.

This is a potential eligible data breach under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Notifiable Data Breaches scheme). Note the **statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy** (in force since June 2025), the expanded civil penalty tiers (including the new mid-tier and lower-tier penalties), and OAIC's increased enforcement posture. Business contact details of ~1,240 individuals, combined with activity data, are personal information; depending on the records, they may be customer-contract data subject to contractual confidentiality and notification obligations (including potentially Bluefen's). A six-week-old "preliminary" investigation is itself a concern: the NDB regime expects assessment within 30 days.

**Position:**
- Pre-Completion covenant: Seller to procure that the Company completes the assessment (and, if required, OAIC and individual notification) before Completion, with the Buyer given the investigation report, the link-recall/access logs, and copies of any notifications.
- Specific warranty on privacy compliance and on this incident (scope, access, notification status).
- Specific indemnity for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident, including regulatory penalties, investigation costs, customer claims, notification costs and remediation, outside the cap/basket/de minimis and with a 6-year time limit.
- Confirm the Company's cyber insurance position and whether the insurer has been notified.

### 3.6 Office lease (DD-007)
Seller frames it as a notification obligation only. Accept the framing provisionally, but: (i) obtain the lease and confirm there is no "change in control" deemed assignment clause (common in commercial leases), (ii) add a Completion deliverable that the required notice has been given, and (iii) warranty that no landlord consent is required and no breach exists.

### 3.7 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – AUD 330,000
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs.
- Disclosure: three related renewals of AUD 110k each; **"read together for timing/scope"**; disclosure silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

The "read together" cue suggests the renewals may have been split to sit under an approval threshold, or that they are timed around Completion. Key questions: are the renewals multi-year commitments, were they entered into after the Accounts date (and so are they leakage or a working-capital point), is there an auto-renewal already triggered, and are they above-market/related-party?

**Position:** Obtain the three renewal documents and supplier relationship details. Treat any commitments entered into between the Accounts date and Completion outside the ordinary course as Leakage / subject to Buyer consent under the pre-Completion conduct covenants. If accrued but unpaid at Completion, they should be in the working-capital/debt-like calculation. Add a warranty on no splitting of contracts to avoid thresholds and that supplier contracts are at arm's length.

### 3.8 Mossvale (DD-009)
Seller says the assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. That is generally correct for a pure anti-assignment clause, but we should read DD-009 ourselves to confirm there is no change-of-control or "deemed assignment" limb. Warranty that no consent is required under any Material Contract other than those listed; indemnity if the Mossvale counterparty terminates on the basis of the transaction.

### 3.9 Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" – **reject**
This is an attempt to fold tax and IP into the 20%/18-month regime. Tax requires a separate Tax Indemnity (pre-Completion tax of the Company, including under any income tax consolidated group exit, GST, payroll tax, stamp duty on the sale, and R&D tax incentive clawbacks given this is an analytics business) with a 100% cap and a 7-year limit. IP needs its own Fundamental-style treatment given the Ironquay point. Also confirm: (i) whether Paperbark is a member of the Harbourglass tax consolidated group and, if so, the clear exit mechanics and tax sharing/funding agreement; (ii) NSW duty position on the share acquisition (landholder duty is unlikely for an analytics business but should be confirmed).

### 3.10 Title (DD-012) – share register only
The Seller's evidence of title is the Company's own share register, and para 10 expressly notes the Buyer has not verified it. We should: (i) obtain an ASIC current extract and compare members/share structure; (ii) obtain the constitution and any shareholders' agreement to check pre-emptive rights and transfer restrictions; (iii) PPSR search against both the Company and Harbourglass for security over the shares (Riverlark may hold a share mortgage); (iv) confirm there are no options, convertible notes, SAFE instruments or employee equity; (v) obtain executed share transfer form, share certificate (or statement of non-issue), and board resolutions approving registration at Completion. Title warranties must be Fundamental (100% cap, 6 years).

## 4. Funds flow and price mechanics

"The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics" is not accurate on the Seller's own disclosure. Debt-free/cash-free means the AUD 24m is an enterprise value to be adjusted at Completion. The draft funds flow omits:
- Riverlark repayment (~AUD 3.2m) – should be a deduction and a direct payment to the bank;
- Closing bonuses and on-costs (~AUD 490k+) – deduction or Seller-paid;
- Potentially the Ironquay SOW3 open amount (AUD 180k) if paid at Completion to perfect IP;
- Any accrued Sandbar liabilities;
- Transaction costs borne by the Company.

We need a locked-box (with leakage protection and a per-diem charge) or completion-accounts mechanism actually drafted into cl. 2/7 with defined Cash, Debt, Debt-like items and Working Capital, and a schedule of agreed Debt-like items. On the current draft we would pay AUD 24m headline and inherit ~AUD 3.9m of debt-like items.
